headline: Revenue growth accelerates, impairments swamp GAAP results
summary_short: Unity's Q1 2026 revenue rose 16.8% y/y to $508.2M on Grow Solutions strength, but GAAP swung to a $347.6M net loss (-$0.80/share) after $279M of impairment charges tied to the ironSource sunset and planned Supersonic divestiture; adjusted EBITDA still grew 64.7% y/y to $138.3M.
summary_long: Revenue growth was driven by Grow Solutions (+23.5% y/y to $351.6M) on Unity Ad Network gains from Vector, partly offset by ironSource declines; Create Solutions rose on subscriptions, offset by lower cloud/hosting revenue from the 2025 portfolio reset. GAAP gross margin fell to 31% from 74% y/y and operating income swung to a loss because $227M of the $279M total impairment hit cost of revenue and $47M hit sales and marketing, tied to the ironSource sunset and planned Supersonic divestiture; adjusted gross margin held flat at 82%. Free cash flow rose to $66.5M from $7.3M y/y. Unity guided Q2 2026 revenue to $505-515M and adjusted EBITDA to $130-135M, and reiterated GAAP profitability by Q4 2026.

drivers.explanation: Revenue growth accelerated on Grow Solutions strength from the Unity Vector product, but GAAP profitability was masked by one-time impairment charges tied to exiting the ironSource Ads Network and divesting Supersonic.

Growth was primarily due to Grow Solutions revenue from Unity Ad Network growth driven by Vector, partially offset by ironSource Ad Network declines, plus higher Create Solutions subscription revenue.
Cost of revenue increased due to a $227M impairment of long-lived intangible assets tied to the ironSource sunset and Supersonic divestiture evaluation, not from underlying cost inflation.
Driven by the $279M total impairment charge ($227M in cost of revenue, $47M in sales and marketing) from sunsetting ironSource and evaluating the Supersonic divestiture.
Tracks the operating-loss swing from impairment charges, partly offset by a larger income-tax benefit from foreign-jurisdiction restructuring activity.
Adjusted EBITDA excludes the impairment, stock-based compensation, and restructuring charges that drove the GAAP net loss, so it reflects the underlying revenue growth and cost discipline.
Higher operating cash flow was primarily due to a decrease in net loss adjusted for non-cash items (impairments, D&A, stock-based compensation) and favorable working-capital timing.
